items.title: SBI expects $10 billion FCNR(B) deposits to support lending, lower funding costs
items.summary: Speaking after the bank announced its first-quarter results, chairman Setty said SBI did not have a specific mobilization target, but the additional funds would help finance loan growth while reducing reliance on expensive bulk deposits.

items.title: Ola Electric’s revenue decline enters 7th quarter; company moves to settle Sebi probe
items.summary: Q1 revenue slumps 45% to  ₹455 crore as the EV maker seeks an early resolution on Sebi’s disclosure probe without admitting liability.

items.title: India’s import dependence continues to be shaped by economic growth, manufacturing base: Govt to Parl
items.summary: India imported goods worth $131.63 billion from China in FY26, accounting for nearly 17% of total merchandise imports, the government told Rajya Sabha. It said Chinese imports include critical minerals, intermediate goods, capital equipment and technologies required by sectors such as clean energy, electronics, pharmaceuticals and infrastructure.

items.title: Hindalco beats Q1 estimates, remains cautious on bauxite auctions
items.summary: The Aditya Birla Group metal flagship reported an almost 75% year-on-year jump in the June-quarter net profit attributable to owners at  ₹7,013 crore.

items.title: Sebi cuts inspection load for market intermediaries, shifts focus to risk-based checks
items.summary: Sebi has overhauled its inspection framework, reducing FY27 inspections to about one-third of last year’s level. The regulator will prioritise risk-based, joint inspections using alerts, complaints and market intelligence while easing compliance burdens for well-governed market intermediaries.

items.title: SBI Q1 profit beats estimates on strong loan growth, asset quality
items.summary: SBI reported a 10% rise in Q1 net profit to Rs 21,121 crore, beating estimates on robust loan growth and higher net interest income. Improved asset quality, lower bad-loan provisions and strong credit demand offset weaker treasury income and slightly lower margins.

items.title: Onion, chicken prices make home-cooked meals costlier in July: Report
items.summary: Vegetarian thali costs rose four percent year-on-year in July. Non-vegetarian thali prices increased nine percent due to higher chicken costs. Onion and vegetable oil prices also contributed significantly to these increases. Potato and tomato prices fell, partially offsetting the overall rise. Month-on-month, vegetarian thali costs saw a two percent jump.

items.title: Onion, LPG prices push home-cooked thali costs up 9% in July: Crisil
items.summary: Onion prices rose 20% year-on-year, while vegetable oil and LPG cylinder prices increased 11% and 10%, respectively.

items.title: India, Russia discuss Vande Bharat, SJ-100 aircraft, UAVs to deepen industrial ties
items.summary: India and Russia reviewed industrial cooperation and explored new collaborations. Discussions focused on railway infrastructure and the Vande Bharat train project. Both nations also discussed opportunities in aircraft production and unmanned aerial systems. Cooperation in critical minerals and lithium mining was a key agenda item. The meeting concluded with a protocol reaffirming deepened bilateral economic ties.

items.title: PE majors Advent, EQT eye Pricol’s smart mobility tech biz
items.summary: Pricol Ltd's plan to spin off its driver information and connected vehicle solutions business has drawn interest from global private equity funds, underscoring the growing appeal of India's automotive electronics sector.

items.title: Hitachi Energy India Q1 Results: Net profit rises over twofold to Rs 294 crore
items.summary: Hitachi Energy India has displayed remarkable financial growth with a net profit soaring over 100% in the June quarter. The company reported a substantial increase in operational revenue compared to the previous year. With first-quarter orders reaching Rs 5,096.5 crore for FY27, the firm has achieved a record order backlog totaling Rs 32,222.1 crore, fueled by robust progress in energy transition and security sectors.

items.title: Gold alone isn't enough for your daughter’s Streedhan. Wealth manager Aarti Gupta explains why
items.summary: Wealth manager Aarti Gupta urged women to diversify beyond physical gold by building goal-based, multi-asset portfolios with SIPs, index funds and ETFs. She also advocated financial independence through personal bank accounts, emergency savings and shared household financial planning.

items.title: BSE Index Services launches BSE REITs Index. Here's everything you need to know
items.summary: BSE Index Services has launched the BSE REITs Index to track the performance of listed Real Estate Investment Trusts in India. The index comprises six REITs and has delivered an 18.54% one-year return on a total-return basis. Embassy Office Parks REIT has the highest weight at 32.18%.

items.title: More exporters leveraging benefits of free trade pacts: Govt
items.summary: In 2025-26, India's ten largest import partner countries were China, UAE, Russia, US, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Hong Kong, Switzerland, Singapore and Japan, as per govt data.

items.title: Market wrap: TCS, SBI, M&M, Trent among top gainers and losers on Nifty and Sensex on Friday
items.summary: Indian equities ended lower as the Closing Auction Session continued creating divergence between Sensex and Nifty. Banking and financial stocks dragged benchmarks, while auto and IT outperformed. Analysts said Nifty’s 24,500 support remains crucial despite easing momentum and continued profit booking.

items.title: Rejected by IIT Madras Computer Science, MIT: How Aravind Srinivas built Perplexity AI
items.summary: Aravind Srinivas, 32, is now an inspiration to anyone facing rejection in competitive examinations, job applications, or other areas of life.

items.title: Apple prices set to stay high until September as Himachal yield drops 30%
items.summary: Climate-driven crop damage in Himachal Pradesh has driven up wholesale prices ahead of the Jammu &amp; Kashmir harvest, prompting traders to turn to imports to plug the supply gap.

items.title: India's forex reserves jump $10.5 billion to over two-month high of $692.87 billion as of July 31
items.summary: India's foreign exchange reserves saw a significant rise of over ten billion dollars. This surge pushed the nation's reserves to their highest point in more than two months. Foreign currency assets, the largest reserve component, increased substantially during the reporting week. Gold reserves also registered a notable gain, contributing to the overall increase. Special Drawing Rights and reserve position with the IMF also saw modest growth.

items.title: Ola Electric Q1 Results: Loss narrows to Rs 336 crore; revenue falls 45% YoY
items.summary: Ola Electric reported a narrower Q1 loss of Rs 336 crore as deliveries nearly doubled sequentially and revenue rebounded 72% from Q4. Improved market share, lower operating costs and progress in battery manufacturing supported the company's operational turnaround despite year-on-year revenue decline.

items.title: Aurobindo Pharma among 8 stocks hitting 52-week highs; surge up to 20% in a month
items.summary: Eight stocks from the BSE 200 index hit fresh 52-week highs, reaching their highest price levels in the past year, indicating strong investor interest, and potential upward momentum in the share price.

items.title: Vikram Solar Q1 net profit declines 85 pc to Rs 20 cr
items.summary: Vikram Solar experienced an astonishing 85 percent drop in profits for the June quarter, primarily attributable to increased expenses. On a positive note, the company's revenue from operations showed a healthy uptick during this period. In a strategic move, Vikram Solar has also greenlit the expansion of its wafer and ingot manufacturing facility, expected to be operational by fiscal year 2029.

items.title: Hero MotoCorp eyes electric motorcycle debut in 2027
items.summary: This marks a first for legacy two-wheeler makers, who have so far stayed away from entering the electric motorcycle segment, even as they work to develop the technology.

items.title: Lupin Q1 PAT rises 16 pc at Rs 1,417 cr
items.summary: Lupin Ltd has reported a remarkable sixteen percent surge in profit after tax for the first quarter, showcasing their continued success. The firm experienced considerable growth in consolidated total revenue from operations, largely driven by a staggering forty-two percent increase in sales in the US market. Moreover, sales in India rose nearly fourteen percent, reflecting strong domestic demand.

items.title: RBI tightens loan recovery rules: EMI defaulters can't be harassed; strict norms on calls and phone-lock tactics
items.summary: Effective 1 January 2027, the new guidelines lay down detailed rules governing how lenders and recovery agents can communicate with borrowers, conduct field visits, and use technology to recover dues.

items.title: L&T Energy bags major offshore project orders from ONGC
items.summary: The awarded projects include the Pipeline Replacement Project and the Well Head Platforms Project

items.title: Won't ease ‘energy drink’ label 90-day deadline — FSSAI says companies should ‘be happy not prosecuting…’: Report
items.summary: In July, the FSSAI privately gave the companies 90 days to drop “energy drink” or any similar description from high-caffeine beverages, saying there were no Indian standards for such products and that using that term breached regulations.

items.title: EXIM Bank to be implementing agency for interest subvention support for exporters: DGFT
items.summary: The commerce ministry announced EXIM Bank will implement export credit interest subvention. This transition from the Reserve Bank of India is effective April 1, 2026. EXIM Bank will manage all operational aspects and claim settlements. The Reserve Bank of India will process claims for the January to March 2026 quarter.

items.title: RBI proposal to curb NBFC revolving credit rattles markets
items.summary: Shares of Bajaj Finance, Tata Capital and Cholamandalam Investment fall 5.8%, 3.2% and 3.8%, respectively, on the NSE.

items.title: Relief for Airtel and Vi as Supreme Court refuses stay on high court's one-time spectrum charge ruling
items.summary: The top court agreed to hear the government's appeal against the verdict quashing retrospective dues, but refused to halt the release of  ₹3,300 crore in bank guarantees to the telecom operators.

items.title: CMS Info Systems bets on tech and payment solutions to drive next growth phase
items.summary: The company aims to double its tech unit's revenue share to over 20% by FY30 by expanding AI surveillance and payment solutions into retail, quick commerce, and EV charging.

items.title: Michael Bloomberg: America needs to repeal rather than just suspend a rusty old shipping law
items.summary: An old law framed to shield the US shipping industry, the Jones Act of 1920, was suspended after the Iran war broke out. That it’s an economic dead-weight is amply clear now that fresh evidence is in. So why not jettison it for good?

items.title: Relief for Dabur as high court stays FSSAI order on ‘100% pure’ claims
items.summary: &nbsp;The court said prima facie it appears the food regulator should not have passed the prohibitory order without first giving Dabur an opportunity to be heard.

items.title: India reviewing bilateral investment treaty overhaul to boost foreign investment: Official
items.summary: India is reviewing its bilateral investment treaty model soon.  The cabinet will decide on changes to attract more foreign capital.  This review comes as India negotiates new pacts with developed nations.  Indian industry bodies also seek faster dispute resolution for investors.  The nation aims to boost foreign direct investment compared to peers.

items.title: RBI allows gradual device restrictions for EMI defaults, eases recovery agent disclosure norms
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India will permit lenders to restrict devices bought on EMI financing.  These restrictions will be gradual and only after a loan is significantly overdue.  Incoming calls and emergency functions will remain accessible to borrowers.  Disclosure requirements for recovery agents have also been eased by the central bank.  The new rules will be implemented from January 1, 2027.

items.title: India's latest trade deals to open new global markets for Arunachal farmers, manufacturers: Piyush Goyal
items.summary: New trade deals offer Arunachal Pradesh farmers and manufacturers global market access.  Nine agreements spanning thirty-eight countries create wider export opportunities for producers.  These pacts aim to lower tariffs and reduce trade barriers for Indian exporters.  Arunachal Pradesh's agriculture and horticulture sectors hold significant export potential.  Strengthening infrastructure and market linkages will boost the state's export growth.

items.title: Indian July consumer inflation likely edged higher on food prices: Reuters poll
items.summary: India’s retail inflation likely rose to 4.50% in July from 4.38% in June, according to a Reuters poll of 40 economists, marking a second straight month above the RBI’s 4% medium-term target.

items.title: A surge of app lending is pushing Indians into a debt trap as they borrow more to repay old loans
items.summary: Loans at an annual rate of 36%? It gets even more usurious in some cases as repayments devour the earnings of those who get tempted by easy app credit to fund consumption and repay loans. This market is a house of cards in need of intervention.

items.title: SC lets Delhi HC continue hearing govt's $2.31 bn claim against Reliance in offshore oilfields dispute
items.summary: The Centre claims Reliance recovered costs in the Panna-Mukta and Tapti offshore oilfields beyond the contractual limit, allowing it to retain more revenue than it was entitled to

items.title: India on track to exceed key fundraising goal on state-firm stake sales
items.summary: India is poised to achieve its divestment aspirations this fiscal year, with enhanced momentum in stake sales and asset monetisation. Although increased fertiliser costs and fuel subsidies pose a challenge to public financial stability due to regional disputes, the country has already garnered over $5.5 billion from diverse stake sales.

items.title: US envoy Sergio Gor meets key industry leaders to advance US-India collaborations
items.summary: US Ambassador Sergio Gor met industry leaders and government officials on Friday. Discussions focused on strengthening US-India collaborations across advanced manufacturing and technology sectors. The critical minerals sector was also a key area for enhancing strategic supply chains between nations. Assistant Secretary Wesley R. Brooks highlighted opportunities in recycling and recovery of critical minerals. The US-India Business Council hosted a roundtable on critical minerals recycling and recovery.

items.title: Malaysia Airlines' parent company MAG orders mandatory drug testing for pilots: Here's what we know
items.summary: Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) has ordered mandatory drug testing and stricter screening for pilots after a Malaysia Airlines pilot was arrested in Indonesia with 26 kg of MDMA.

items.title: Vedanta tops bidding for Karlapat bauxite block with record 175% premium
items.summary: The outcome of the Karlapat bauxite block auction is significant, as aluminium makers and new entrants alike compete to secure long-term access to the mineral amid an aggressive capacity expansion cycle.

items.title: RBI's FCNR(B) scheme attracts $41 billion, Jefferies says inflows may double to $80-100 billion
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India's deposit scheme has attracted significant foreign currency inflows.  This scheme is expected to mobilize up to one hundred billion dollars by its closing date.  These inflows are helping to stabilize the Indian rupee after a period of weakness.  Additionally, tax-free government bonds are attracting foreign investment and improving capital flows.

items.title: The CEO premium: FMCG's hunt for talent drives executive pay
items.summary: Indian consumer goods firms reported high CEO remuneration and new appointments in FY26, as they sought experienced leaders to manage market challenges

items.title: IndiaRF acquires majority stake in Fine Edge Engineering for about  ₹2,000 crore
items.summary: India Resurgence Fund has acquired a majority stake in Ashok Iron Works' engineering business, betting on rising demand for large engine components amid the global manufacturing and data centre boom.

items.title: RBI gives Urban Cooperative Banks new lease of life | Explained
items.summary: Reigniting the cooperative banking sector, which went through a painful course correction, is a logical step to deepen financial inclusion as MSMEs continue to face credit gaps despite digital lenders’ growth

items.title: FAA directs Boeing to inspect hundreds of 737 Max jets over possible cracks: How many are active in India?
items.summary: The FAA on Thursday (local time) ordered inspections of 471 Boeing 737 Max jets over concerns about possible cracks in a structural component. Boeing said it supports the directive and is working on fixes. The order comes amid past safety scrutiny of the aircraft

items.title: It’s time for India’s Unified Payments Interface to fund itself—without burdening people at large
items.summary: Public infrastructure attracts capital if users are ready to pay fair and transparent usage charges. In the case of NPCI’s UPI too, the user-pays principle should apply. Let the Reserve Bank of India’s e-rupee serve as the country’s digital cash.

items.title: Mint Quick Edit | Questions of legal liability for insults to national honour demand wide deliberation
items.summary: Indian Parliament amended a law to expand what forms of national honour mustn’t be violated. Its implementation, however, would likely risk causing a conflict of conscience among some folks. On such matters, it’s best to let consensus prevail.

items.title: Storage, transmission key for next phase of India's energy transition: Experts
items.summary: Stakeholders at the Mint Sustainability Summit 2026 say transmission bottlenecks, battery storage and regulatory reforms will determine the next phase of India's renewable energy growth.

items.title: JSW Steel and Tata Steel choose different growth paths—one bets on scale, the other on value
items.summary: While JSW Steel is expanding its production capacity aggressively through new projects and joint ventures, Tata Steel is betting on higher-margin, value-added products. Their strategies are more nuanced than stark and present different choices being made in a red-hot market for steel.

items.title: Tariff rationalisation set to continue, more steps likely in FY28 Budget: FM
items.summary: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman confirmed ongoing import tariff rationalisation efforts.  Further measures are expected in the budget for the year 2027-28.  She also outlined the Viksit Bharat vision for the year 2047.  This vision includes zero poverty and universal access to education and healthcare.  India's destiny is to become a developed civilisation with prosperity and responsibility.

items.title: India can raise per capita income six-fold by '47: NITI Vice Chairman
items.summary: India's per capita income could rise six-fold by 2047. This growth would make the nation a developed economy. Higher investment and domestic savings are critical for sustained economic growth. Structural reforms are needed to remove investment obstacles. Achieving this goal requires attracting investment and boosting savings.

items.title: Zero poverty, education, jobs core of Viksit Bharat plan, says Sitharaman
items.summary: Finance minister also outlined the government's vision of zero poverty, universal access to quality education, affordable and comprehensive healthcare for every citizen.

items.title: Parl panel for early conclusion of India-US trade pact, tariff exemptions on key goods
items.summary: The panel suggested the commerce department prepare a time-bound roadmap to achieve the objectives of the Mission 500 initiative by promoting trade in goods and services, encouraging investment, enhancing cooperation in critical technologies, improving supply chain and addressing both tariff and non-tariff barriers faced by Indian exporters  and prepare a long-term strategy to increase India's share in the American market. The two countries aim to more than double total bilateral trade to $500 billion by 2030.

items.title: India may rationalise most customs tariffs by Budget 2027-28, Nirmala Sitharaman says
items.summary: India's finance minister announced plans to streamline customs tariffs, aiming for a significant overhaul by the fiscal year 2027-28. This move is expected to simplify trade procedures and potentially boost economic activity by making imports and exports more predictable and cost-effective for businesses across various sectors.

items.title: India, Brazil must join hands to defend multilateralism amid tariffs: Brazilian Trade Minister Márcio Fernando Elias Rosa
items.summary: Brazil's Industry Minister urged India to jointly defend multilateralism and the WTO.  He highlighted the need to counter unilateral tariff impositions by the United States.  Brazil seeks to diversify export markets, with India being a key priority.  Brazilian companies are also keen to invest in Indian energy and infrastructure projects.  Cooperation on fertilizer supply and green ammonia for agriculture is also sought.

items.title: India-Israel investment agreement in force: Modi, Netanyahu discuss enhanced bilateral ties
items.summary: Prime Minister Modi and Israeli PM Netanyahu discussed bilateral progress and a new investment agreement. This agreement, effective Saturday, aims to boost investment and protect investors. It allows three years for local dispute resolution before international arbitration. The leaders reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation across various sectors. They also exchanged views on recent developments in West Asia and agreed to stay in touch.

items.title: How—and how much—should central banks talk?
items.summary: For much of the 20th century central bankers cultivated a similar mystique. Their authority rested on the impression that they were omniscient and omnipotent. Since in truth they were neither, obscurantism was useful.

items.title: Indian rice export prices near 10-month high amid El Nino fears and rising domestic paddy costs
items.summary: Indian rice export prices remain near a ten-month high this week. Thai prices have reached a one-month peak, supported by buyer demand. Vietnam's rice exports are experiencing quiet trading activity due to weak demand. Bangladesh faces elevated rice prices after recent crop damage from flooding. Governments are developing climate-resilient rice varieties to address agricultural challenges.

items.title: Bitter pill: Govt to debar firms submitting fake data for drug approvals
items.summary: This assumes significant for India's $60-billion pharmaceutical market, as the government aims to clean up the approval system and ensure drug safety and quality.

items.title: India needs to ease land acquisition process for industries to attract investments: NITI vice-chairman
items.summary: NITI Aayog's Ashok Kumar Lahiri highlighted easing land acquisition for industrial investment. He stressed the need for increased domestic savings to fund national growth. Public investment now complements private investment, unlocking further economic potential. India's per capita income must grow significantly to reach developed status by 2047. Government schemes aim to promote entrepreneurship, invention, and innovation across the nation.

items.title: Lok Sabha passes Bill enabling Centre to allow UPI charges, MDR on digital payments
items.summary: The Lok Sabha approved amendments to the Payment and Settlement Systems Act. This change empowers the government to permit charges on digital payment transactions. Currently, UPI transactions remain free for users and merchants. Banks and payment firms seek sustainable revenue models for infrastructure. The government will decide which digital payment methods may attract future charges.

items.title: Lopsided GST flexibility: India needs to resolve a stark asymmetry in this tax regime
items.summary: In India, the state has granted itself wide leeway on GST implementation timelines, but offers taxpayers no respite. While income-tax officials have the discretion to pardon delays by taxpayers who cite good reasons, GST doesn’t. This needs fixing.

items.title: One in 3 Indian companies skipped mandatory filings, clouding corporate records
items.summary: Legal experts attributed the decline in compliance to a combination of dormant and inactive companies, financial stress and rising compliance challenges, particularly for smaller businesses.

items.title: AI movies aren't all slop—for some aspiring filmmakers they can be empowering
items.summary: Filmmaking is an art of storytelling that AI could surely help sharpen. It also opens this art form up to those with modest budgets. Just as human involvement doesn't guarantee artistry, AI assistance needn’t translate into soulless slop.

items.title: Mint Explainer | Why food labelling is under the FSSAI scanner
items.summary: Rising consumer demand for healthier foods, stricter enforcement and misleading claims are forcing companies to rethink packaging as the FSSAI steps up scrutiny.

items.title: Lok Sabha passes Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill to boost foreign investment, electronics manufacturing
items.summary: The Lok Sabha passed a bill to attract foreign investment and promote domestic manufacturing. This legislation aims to provide greater tax certainty for businesses operating in India. It simplifies tax frameworks for offshore investment funds and fund managers. The bill also extends tax exemptions for electronics manufacturing and diamond trade.

items.title: Mint Explainer | Why India wants vehicles to ‘talk’ to each other
items.summary: Vehicle-to-vehicle systems allow vehicles to exchange information on speed, position, direction and acceleration in real time, preventing collisions. What does the Centre's mandate on the system mean for the future of mobility in India?

items.title: Disaster display: the Assam floods reveal India’s outdated apparatus of climate finance
items.summary: Climate risk varies by river basins, but governance and finance are sliced up by administrative boundaries. This mismatch is smaller than the one in how funds are devolved to states. For anticipatory funding, here’s how Indian policy must evolve.

items.title: When is your home loan EMI increasing? RBI rate hike calls pushed back after  dovish pause
items.summary: Economists now anticipate the Reserve Bank of India will raise rates in December or later. This shift occurs as core inflation remains low, contrary to earlier expectations. The central bank maintained its current rates and lowered inflation forecasts for this fiscal year. Overnight indexed swap rates also signal fewer rate hikes over the next twelve months. India's monetary policy stance differs from other Asian economies responding to oil price spikes.

items.title: India's big billion-dollar trade deals are done. Now comes the real test
items.summary: India has spent years negotiating free trade agreements with some of the world's biggest economies. But signing the deals was only half the battle. The bigger challenge now is helping Indian businesses turn preferential market access into exports, investments, manufacturing growth and global competitiveness.

items.title: Employment anxiety: India needs jobs that offer a decent living wage and social security
items.summary: The country's employment statistics show new jobs being created, but many were in agriculture—a reversal of the shift away from farms any emerging economy sees. Meanwhile, euphoria over India’s rapid economic growth has stoked aspirations.

items.title: Bollywood’s family comeback: Old-school entertainers bring audiences back to theatres
items.summary: Family audiences are returning to cinemas—but only for films that feel worth the outing. Industry experts say strong content, event films and premium experiences are driving the revival.

items.title: How market participants read RBI's order of priority has a bearing on how well monetary policy works
items.summary: The decision to hold India’s policy rate steady in the face of inflation risks felt like a foregone conclusion. Now that RBI watchers appear to have assumed a hierarchy of policy goals, India’s central bank must mull over the potential consequences.

items.title: India-Sri Lanka focus on infrastructure projects; updating FTA to boost Comprehensive Partnership
items.summary: Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri met Sri Lankan leaders to review bilateral cooperation and projects. Agreements were finalized on social security and Indian Rupee-denominated credit lines for infrastructure. Discussions advanced updating the Free Trade Agreement and energy project implementation. Progress was noted on housing and disaster warning systems for Sri Lanka. Both nations affirmed commitment to security and a mutually beneficial development partnership.

items.title: Highs and lows: On GST metrics
items.summary: GST must be fuelled by domestic production, not inflation or imports

items.title: India’s new 15-year tax break could unlock global rough diamond trade
items.summary: India is closer to becoming a global rough diamond hub. A new tax exemption will attract foreign companies to trade rough diamonds. This measure offers a 15-year income tax holiday for eligible firms. It aims to boost trading activity within India's Special Notified Zones. The government's move is expected to enhance India's diamond industry competitiveness.

items.title: ‘Lifeline for North Mumbai’: Goyal sets deadline for Bandra-Versova-Bhayander Coastal Road project
India's economic growth may moderate in H2FY27, accelerate to 7.2% in FY28: Report
items.summary: India's economic growth will likely moderate in the second half of FY27. Growth may strengthen to around 7.2 per cent in FY28, says ICICI Bank. The Monetary Policy Committee kept the repo rate unchanged at 5.25 per cent. Most high-frequency indicators point to robust growth in the first quarter. RBI sees risks to both growth and inflation as evenly balanced.

items.title: India, Africa powerful force for global progress: Jaishankar
items.summary: India's External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar highlighted Africa as a priority partner. He stated Africa's due place is essential for a multipolar world order. The minister expressed India's commitment to strengthening ties with the African Union. He looked forward to reconvening the deferred India-Africa Forum Summit. Human resource development remains central to this vital engagement.

items.title: Will retail investors bear the brunt of a shift in India’s stock market formula for end-of-day price discovery?
items.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India's (Sebi) attempt to improve how the country's stock market functions by altering how closing prices are determined has led to spasms of volatility. The new formula has its merits, but wasn’t it tested out in advance?

items.title: Mint Quick Edit | The monetary policy committee's inflation hypothesis will be tested this year
items.summary: India’s central bank held its policy rate and stance steady, but the variable it must hold within a tight band is retail inflation. Did advocates of an inflation-targeting regime over-estimate its role in assuring the country price stability?

items.title: Short holiday, strong demand: Drive-to escapes lead Independence Day travel
items.summary: Travellers are swapping fly-to vacations for road trips and staycations, with hotel chains and villa operators reporting bookings ahead of last year despite the compressed holiday calendar.

items.title: India's two-wheeler makers restructure, gear up for EV and premium shift
items.summary: Top two-wheeler makers such as Hero MotoCorp, Bajaj Auto and TVS Motor are undertaking several measures, including integrating their EV businesses with core two-wheeler operations, creating dedicated leadership roles for high-growth segments and rolling out exclusive retail networks to boost sales.

items.title: RBI holds repo rate at 5.25%, raises FY27 growth forecast, cuts inflation outlook
items.summary: The RBI kept the repo rate unchanged at 5.25% for the fourth straight policy review, retained its neutral stance, raised its FY27 growth forecast to 6.7%, and lowered the inflation projection to 5%. It also announced revised loan pricing norms, plans to resume urban cooperative bank licences, and expressed confidence in India's economic resilience despite global uncertainties.

items.title: India to probe Chinese link in solar-cell import surge from Ethiopia
items.summary: India may investigate whether existing trade rules are being circumvented.

items.title: New framework to standardise interest rate rules on the anvil, says RBI
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India plans to standardize interest rate rules for all regulated entities. This new principle-based framework aims to increase transparency and ensure uniformity across lending. The proposed changes are unlikely to affect EMIs or bring NBFCs into the external benchmark regime. Governor Sanjay Malhotra stated this move will improve consumer protection and rationalise existing norms.

items.title: Govt mandates exporter registration for FDI-backed ecommerce inventory exports
items.summary: Foreign-invested ecommerce firms must register as exporter-on-record for export inventory. These companies can only procure and stock goods against confirmed export orders. Speculative stockpiling for future outbound shipping will not be allowed by the government. Indian sellers can access overseas markets by delegating export tasks to the exporter-on-record. This framework aims to boost India's export capabilities and ensure timely payments.

items.title: Govt drafts customs playbook for 100 imports to streamline FTA benefits
items.summary: The government is creating a customs playbook for key imported goods. This initiative aims to standardize the faceless customs regime across India. It will reduce disputes and speed up clearance times for businesses. The playbook will help companies utilize free trade agreement benefits effectively. This reform seeks to improve ease of doing business and trade efficiency.

items.title: India's services growth slows to 4½-year low in July as demand weakens
items.summary: India's services sector expanded slowly in July, reaching a 53-month low. New business inflows moderated across domestic and international markets, impacting growth. Manufacturing activity also lost momentum, contributing to a composite PMI decline. Services firms remained optimistic about future business despite current slowdowns. Hiring showed a modest rebound as input cost inflation eased.

items.title: India’s fertiliser imports, production plunge as West Asia war drives costs
items.summary: India's fertilizer production and imports have fallen sharply in the June quarter. This decline is due to inflated raw material prices caused by the West Asia conflict. Production of complex fertilizers dropped twenty-eight percent, and imports slipped forty-eight point five percent. Ammonia and sulphur prices have nearly doubled, making manufacturing and imports less viable. This situation raises concerns over nutrient availability for the ongoing crop sowing season.

items.title: NITI Aayog calls for national caregiving framework, social security for caregivers
items.summary: NITI Aayog suggests a dedicated policy framework for India's growing ageing population.  It calls for regulating the caregiving ecosystem and setting essential caregiving standards.  The report proposes financial incentives and entrepreneurship opportunities for caregivers to boost scalability.  It also recommends introducing care leave for employees supporting dependent parents.  Establishing a National Caregiving Council will provide institutional leadership and coordination.

items.title: Centre sustains capex push in Q1 despite global trade disruptions, geopolitical uncertainty
items.summary: The infrastructure-led growth strategy has remained at the centre of India’s fiscal policy over the past several years and economists assert that public investment in productive assets has a larger multiplier effect than revenue spending.

items.title: Trai moves to stop 5G fast lanes from slowing other users
items.summary: Draft quality-of-service rules would require operators to add capacity and remove overloaded cells from network slicing to protect service quality for all users.

items.summary: It is true that there is an increase in carbon emission by India and China due to homegrown consumption and lack of infrastructure. But let#39;s keep in mind that India#39;s carbon emissions per capita are still 10 times lower and China#39;s is half of that compared to the US.
